posts.title: Challenging The Tides: “Hull’s Teeth”
posts.description: When Shellie Horst first broached the idea of producing an anthology of hopepunk stories set around the Humber, I was assailed by two conflicting emotions. Excitement at the prospect of being part of a project that featured northern writers with stories based in my local area, and a sense of flailing personal doubt. How was I going to write a story with a hopeful ending in these difficult times? It was a challenge. As I pursued the threads of the story, I realised that the core had to be one of community spirit. I know that sounds clichéd, but consider, along with the disasters affecting so many areas around the world there are equally striking accounts of people working together to ensure the survival and well-being of all. One of my favourite authors in the hopepunk genre is Becky Chambers whose work is both thought provoking and comforting.
